title: OECD Raises 2026 Global Growth Forecast to 2.9%, Says World Economy Absorbed Middle East Energy Shock Better Than Expected
detail: The OECD's September Interim Economic Outlook raised its 2026 global GDP growth projection to 2.9% (up 0.1 point from June) and forecast 3.0% for 2027, concluding the world economy 'has weathered the energy supply shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East better than expected' thanks to government support measures, alternative energy supply from outside the Gulf, drawdowns of oil reserves, and continued AI-driven investment. Country-level detail: US growth was revised up 0.2 points to 2.2%, the eurozone up 0.2 points to 1.0%, and China held steady at 4.5%; G20 headline inflation is projected at 4.1% for the year. OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann and Chief Economist Stefano Scarpetta, presenting the outlook, flagged three key downside risks: a prolonged Middle East conflict, weather-related supply shocks from a strong El Niño, and AI investment returns that fail to meet expectations — plus rising long-term sovereign bond yields straining public finances in heavily indebted economies.

sources.name: Euronews — OECD Lifts 2026 Global Economic Growth Forecast to 2.9% Despite Iran War Disruption
OECD — Global Growth Holds Up Despite Successive Shocks, but Risks Persist

media.caption: The OECD's September Interim Economic Outlook lifted its 2026 global growth forecast to 2.9%, citing resilience to the Middle East energy shock

title: Bessent Says US and China Extend 'Busan Agreement' Trade Truce to January 10, 2027, Ahead of Xi's Washington Visit
detail: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the US and China agreed to extend the 'Busan Agreement' — the trade détente reached at the October 30, 2025 Busan summit — by roughly two months, from its original November 10, 2026 expiration to January 10, 2027. The framework had reduced the average US tariff rate on Chinese imports from 57% to 47% (with fentanyl-linked punitive tariffs cut from 20% to 10%), suspended retaliatory Chinese tariffs and rare-earth/high-tech export controls for a year, and secured Chinese agricultural purchase commitments. The extension came a day after Bessent and USTR Jamieson Greer held 'successful' pre-summit talks in New York with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng on AI, tariffs and critical minerals, and just ahead of Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington for a summit with President Trump. Bessent indicated some Chinese compliance with existing terms still needed improvement, and floated further expansion into agricultural purchases, financial services, consumer goods, energy and medical devices, plus a new bilateral AI-safety notification mechanism.
